clue.text: Register one proverbially sick?

definitions.meaning: to register a vote, or to record people's opinions in a survey
the idiom 'sick as a parrot' means bitterly disappointed

explanation.surface: A question about recording someone in a register who is famous for being ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick as a parrot' is a British football-pundit cliché for being gutted after a defeat; Poll (as in 'Pretty Polly') is the stock parrot's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To register votes or opinions is to take a survey of them, a standard verb sense; the second reading names the stock parrot.

clue.text: Louder support not coming to an end

indicators.note: the support word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a bra, in full a brassiere, is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a noisier backing never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass instruments are loud and blaring, so brassier describes a harsher, noisier sound, a comparative adjective.

clue.text: Like one learning in small group maybe, mostly perceptive

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.words: one learning in small group maybe
parts.note: a tutee is a student taught in a tutorial, typically a small group

explanation.surface: A description of a sharp-witted student taught in a tutorial group.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and perceptive are synonyms, both meaning shrewd and quick to notice things.

clue.text: Being made up — the tricks one will need to get smart!

parts.note: cons are confidence tricks, swindles
I is the Roman numeral one
to smart is to sting, as a wound does

explanation.surface: A con artist muses that clever swindles and a single person are needed to get clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective meaning clever but is the verb meaning to hurt sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: Consisting of means made up of or composed of, so the participle matches the phrase.

clue.text: US broadcast against imperial measure by implication?

definitions.meaning: a show on radio or television, in American spelling
being pro (in favour of) the gram, a metric weight, implies opposing imperial units like ounces

explanation.surface: An American transmission campaigning against old-fashioned pounds and ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it 3,4: PRO GRAM, supporting the metric gram, which by implication sets one against imperial measure.
explanation.definitionFit: American English spells the British 'programme' without the final letters, meaning a broadcast show.

clue.text: Head belting learner to make an impression

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a thing used to print; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: the head word wraps round the learner like a belt fastened round the waist

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
L is the learner-driver ... abbreviation

explanation.surface: A violent picture of a headteacher hitting a pupil to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing plate is the engraved sheet used to press an image onto paper, so it makes an impression.

clue.text: Bungling fellow taking time, leading others in haze

indicators.note: the whole run of pieces sits within the haze word

parts.note: mist is a light haze

indicators.note: the fellow takes on time after it, the two placed together
the first pieces come ahead of the others in order

parts.note: a fellow is a man
an age is a long period of time
other chaps, men

explanation.surface: A man fumbles about lost in fog, holding up his time and leading other people astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Bungling, as a noun, is clumsy mishandling, a synonym of poor administration of affairs.

clue.text: Time to leave second home for one wanting to explore?

indicators.note: the time word departs from the home word

parts.note: a cottage is a small country home
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone muses that it is time to quit a holiday cottage and go travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Robert Falcon Scott led the ill-fated British expedition to the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott was a celebrated polar explorer, so the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: River beside NJ city

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
on can mean next to, as in a town on the coast

explanation.surface: A river runs alongside a city in New Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the state capital of New Jersey, abbreviated NJ, an example of a city there.

clue.text: Skin problem? We'd like to hear from you

definitions.meaning: a patch of thickened hardened skin, as on a hand or foot

definitions.text: We'd like to hear from you
definitions.meaning: a request to phone us, as in an advertisement inviting contact

explanation.surface: A dermatology clinic advert inviting people with skin complaints to get in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 4,2 the answer is an invitation to telephone; as one word it is hardened skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardened thickened patch of skin is a dermatological complaint, and the split phrase is an advertising invitation to telephone.

clue.text: The woman surrounded by group of soldiers is humiliated

indicators.note: the woman is enclosed by the soldiers on both sides

parts.note: a squad is a small unit of soldiers
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman hemmed in by a band of troops is put to shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Squashed can mean crushed or put down, as by a crushing retort, so humiliated is a synonym.

clue.text: Restore the empty vicar with tea possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way
an emptied word keeps only its outside letters, its inside removed

explanation.surface: A cheerful suggestion that a cup of tea might revive an exhausted vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TE from 'the'; 'possibly' then rearranges TE + VICAR + TEA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reactivate something is to bring it back into action, a close synonym of restore.

clue.text: Report of European corporation gathering in place at international border?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the European word is given by its sound

parts.note: a Czech is a native of the Czech Republic in Europe

indicators.note: the belly word gathers the next word into itself

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a pot

explanation.surface: A news report about a European company's meeting at a frontier town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' here is the dated humorous term for a big stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A border post where travellers are stopped and inspected sits at a frontier, so it fits the definition by example.

clue.text: Asian meat dish odd number (not even) consumed

indicators.note: the odd number goes without its even part

parts.note: seven is an odd number
the word even itself is spelt out and taken away
ate means consumed, eaten

explanation.surface: A description of a skewer of Asian meat, picking an odd number and eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not even' strips EVEN from SEVEN, leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Saté, often spelt satay, is a Southeast Asian dish of grilled skewered meat with peanut sauce.

clue.text: A screaming loony grabs a politician in attempt to bring discredit

indicators.note: the jumbled letters seize the next pieces and hold them inside
loony means crazy, so these letters are set in a mad new order

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A shrieking lunatic seizes a politician in a bid to disgrace someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loony' makes SMEARCAIGN; the capital A at the start belongs to the jumbled letters, while the second 'a' joins the politician in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear campaign is an organised effort to damage a rival's reputation with rumours, an idiom for the phrase given.

clue.text: There's nothing for one in wicked things, slobs!

indicators.note: the nothing word stands in place of the one

parts.note: sins are wicked acts
I is the Roman numeral one
love means nothing or zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A moralist declares there is no excuse for slovenly people's wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts LOVE in place of the I in SINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovens are untidy, careless people, so they are slobs, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Home overlooking harbour area is where Arabs may gather

indicators.note: in a down answer the home sits above the harbour, looking down on it

parts.note: a pad is informal for one's flat or home
the docks are the wharf area of a harbour

explanation.surface: A house with a view over the docks, where Arab traders might meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs here are the horse breed, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddocks are small fields where horses, such as the Arab breed, are kept or assembled before racing.

clue.text: What may be interpreted as royalist tool?

definitions.text: What may be interpreted as royalist
definitions.meaning: split 3,1 the letters say in favour of a king, using K for king
a pronged implement for eating or for gardening

explanation.surface: A question about an implement that might be taken as backing the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronged implement for digging or eating is a basic tool, and the split reading backs the king.

clue.text: Gets endless grub, ye'd fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are given an elaborate rearrangement
the word grub loses its final letter, having no end

explanation.surface: You would imagine a glutton keeps getting an unending supply of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts B off 'grub'; 'fancy' rearranges GETS + GRU + YED. The whole clue describes a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy guts is a British informal term for a glutton, who would indeed get endless food.

clue.text: Good music-maker offering bits of rock

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A fine musician offers bits of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like the music genre beside 'music-maker', but it is stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel is a mass of small stones, literally fragments of rock used for paths.

clue.text: Moulding a group of stars in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Taurus is the constellation of the Bull

explanation.surface: A theatre decorated with plasterwork, or a troupe of celebrities appearing there.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a torus is a large convex rounded moulding at the base of a column.

clue.text: Give a lecture that's riddle without sounding loud

indicators.note: the loud letter is not voiced, so it goes out

parts.note: to riddle is to pierce with many holes
F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud

explanation.surface: A speaker delivers a talk on a puzzle while keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the verb meaning to pepper with holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To perorate is to speak at length in a grand manner, or to sum up a speech, so it means to lecture.

clue.text: Old car that's kept by city producing different make

indicators.note: the car word keeps the by letter next to it, held in the answer before it

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in three by four
Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A vintage car kept in a city where a rival brand is made.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris cars, including the Morris Oxford, were made at Cowley in Oxford, a make different from Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is the English city where Morris cars were built, a different make from the Ford in the wordplay.

clue.text: Scandinavian hero of American fiction

definitions.meaning: a native of Finland, in the Nordic region
Huckleberry ... is Mark Twain's boy hero

explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a person from Finland, loosely grouped with Scandinavians, and Huck Finn is Twain's hero.

clue.text: Result of match accident? One will get left out

indicators.note: will get ... out says the left letter is pushed out of the one word
this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A sporting match goes wrong when one player is dropped from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks sporting but is a match that is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorch mark is what a struck match can leave on careless contact, a singe.

clue.text: Casual acknowledgement to Magi for gold received?

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
the Magi are the three kings of the Nativity story

explanation.surface: An informal thank-you to the Three Wise Men for their gift of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi brought gold, frankincense and myrrh, so 'gold received' looks like the gift but means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are money received by a shop or business, and gold stands loosely for money.
